evidence.exact_quote: The PlanUnit index phase ends at node-readiness reporting. It may analyze blockers, missing dependencies, validation coverage, risk, ambiguity, context scope, implementation surfaces, and gui_related routing inheritance. Runtime PlanCompile is a separate implementation surface: it can draft non-executable NodeSeed candidates, certify a WorkGraph draft, emit WorkNodeRequest records for Executor intake, and materialize WorkNodeRecord objects only after activation. The indexer itself does not create final WorkNodes or executable build tasks.

items.impact: This explicit separation prevents analysis and governance generation from being mistaken for authorization to create executable work.
items.statement: The prologue and PNC-001 consistently terminate indexing at readiness analysis and reserve runtime artifacts for PlanCompile, Executor intake, activation, and certification.
items.title: Indexing and execution are explicitly separated

evidence.exact_quote: - Missing compiler-critical metadata is reported as node-readiness blocker, not silently inferred.

items.impact: Compiler-critical omissions have a fail-closed disposition instead of becoming hidden builder assumptions.
items.statement: PNC-002 defines the metadata inputs and explicitly requires missing critical metadata to block readiness rather than be inferred.
items.title: Compiler metadata omissions fail closed

evidence.exact_quote: - PlanUnits do not hardcode model names as canonical execution policy.

items.impact: Capability requirements remain durable while provider and model resolution can evolve at runtime.
items.statement: PNC-003 assigns Plans authority over capability and ordering metadata while withholding authority to hardcode runtime model selection.
items.title: Plans express capability, not provider policy

evidence.exact_quote: - compile_wave_retry_route uses the schema enum values and records route_kind, reason_code, failed_plan_unit_ids[], retry_after_ms?, and owner_doc_refs[].

items.impact: Implementers and validators cannot know whether compile_wave_retry_route uses reason_code and failed PlanUnit routing fields or the target_stage, reason, and resume_ref shape later specified by PNC-010, risking incompatible persisted receipts and retry behavior.
items.statement: PNC-023 describes compile_wave_retry_route with route_kind, reason_code, failed_plan_unit_ids, retry_after_ms, and owner_doc_refs, while PNC-010 describes the same canonical object with route_kind, target_stage, reason, and optional resume_ref.
items.title: Compile-wave retry route has conflicting shapes

evidence.exact_quote: - Buildability report remains blocked while PNC-019 executable lifecycle certification is incomplete.

items.impact: The gate can project inconsistent status for an intentionally disabled runtime because PNC-021 requires lifecycle certification to clear buildability while PNC-019 later allows intentional disablement as an alternative to a passing harness.
items.statement: PNC-021 does not define a non-applicable or disabled terminal state that reconciles its hard block with PNC-019's intentionally-disabled alternative.
items.title: Disabled runtime gate semantics are contradictory

evidence.exact_quote: - The bootstrap authority does not set buildability_gate_passed=true and does not enable Planning Wizard Approve And Build for ordinary product work.

items.impact: Bootstrap work can make the lifecycle certifiable without silently widening into ordinary product execution authority.
items.statement: PNC-022 narrowly scopes bootstrap authorization to the certification harness and keeps it distinct from runtime enablement and ordinary-product WorkNode permission.
items.title: Bootstrap authority is bounded and non-transitive

evidence.exact_quote: - If the PlanCompile compiler contract is incomplete, readiness status records blocked_compiler_contract_incomplete; once PNC-007 is accepted, runtime_enablement_status records the compiler contract as complete, but readiness remains blocked_runtime_certification_incomplete until the PNC-019 executable lifecycle certification harness passes and records evidence.

items.impact: Consumers can distinguish a complete compiler specification from executable lifecycle proof and avoid a misleading ready state.
items.statement: PNC-004 defines separate blocked states for incomplete Plans, incomplete compiler contract, and incomplete runtime certification.
items.title: Readiness state separates specification from execution proof

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Future NodeSeeds and WorkNodes inherit gui_related from source PlanUnits. If gui_related is true and separate GUI model routing is enabled, the orchestrator routes the task to the configured GUI-capable model or CLI; otherwise it uses the default model.

items.impact: When GUI routing is enabled but the configured GUI-capable provider is unavailable, unauthorized, or lacks required capabilities, silently using the default model could violate user intent and produce unsuitable GUI work.
items.statement: PNC-005 defines the disabled-policy fallback but not the failure state, receipt, escalation, or fail-closed behavior for an enabled GUI route whose configured target cannot be used.
items.title: GUI routing failure behavior is unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Future Planning Wizard uses native Goal Mode invisibly for ledger-to-Plans transfer, Plans-to-node conversion after this compiler contract is complete, and audit. Assistant chat can invoke Goal Mode visibly for arbitrary execution tasks.

items.impact: An invisible invocation has no locally stated user-facing status, cancellation, failure disclosure, or receipt contract, leaving consumers unable to distinguish progress, retry, and terminal failure.
items.statement: PNC-006 assigns native Goal Mode to invisible Planning Wizard operations but specifies only the phase boundary, not the observability and control contract for that invisibility.
items.title: Invisible Goal handoff lacks a visible control contract

evidence.exact_quote: - The report explicitly states no_worknodes_created=true for index generation even when the compiler contract is complete.

items.impact: A machine-checkable negative assertion prevents readiness output from being presented as evidence of generated execution artifacts.
items.statement: PNC-008 requires the generated report to expose blockers, routing inheritance, runtime enablement status, and an explicit no-worknodes assertion.
items.title: Readiness report includes a negative creation oracle

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime PlanCompile is accepted as an implementation contract by a deterministic PlanUnit to NodeSeed to WorkGraph to WorkNodeRequest to Executor intake boundary.

items.impact: The accepted algorithm has ordered inputs, exclusions, review and certification gates, and an explicit activation boundary that blocks direct compiler dispatch.
items.statement: PNC-007 defines a deterministic PlanUnit-to-NodeSeed-to-WorkGraph-to-WorkNodeRequest pipeline whose runtime artifact materialization depends on Executor intake, activation, and executable lifecycle certification.
items.title: Compiler algorithm has an explicit activation boundary

evidence.exact_quote: - Missing executable compiler schema keeps NodeSeeds, WorkNodes, executable queues, final node manifests, final build tasks, and production build tasks absent.

items.impact: Orchestrator-facing projections may display owner state without gaining creation authority through terminology or UI presence.
items.statement: PNC-009 cleanly distinguishes design-time references and projections from runtime artifact creation.
items.title: Orchestrator projections do not confer runtime authority

evidence.exact_quote: retry_route uses the canonical compile_wave_retry_route object with route_kind, target_stage, reason, and optional resume_ref rather than free-form strings; target_stage is a stage_name, except terminal route kinds must use null.

items.impact: The PNC-010 route shape cannot be reconciled from this document with PNC-023's different required fields, so persistence, validation, and resumption may disagree.
items.statement: PNC-010's canonical compile_wave_retry_route shape directly conflicts with PNC-023's shape for the identically named object.
items.title: PNC-010 confirms the retry-route contradiction

evidence.exact_quote: Required stage contracts use the canonical registry: preflight_currentness, scope_selection, planunit_normalization, test_repository_discovery, typed_dependency_analysis, implementation_surface_mapping, work_risk_classification, nodeseed_candidate_drafting, split_merge_sizing, candidate_review, workgraph_construction, worknode_request_construction, final_compile_audit_repair, executor_handoff_certification, activation_transaction, and orchestrator_projection.

items.impact: Durable runs persisted under one registry revision have no specified upgrade, alias, rejection, or supersession behavior when stage names or ordering evolve.
items.statement: PNC-011 defines an exact stage registry and resumable state but does not state a registry version or migration rule for already-persisted runs.
items.title: Stage-card registry lacks migration semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - NodeSeed candidates are explicitly non-executable and cannot be dispatched.

items.impact: Candidate generation and review remain safe, reviewable planning operations rather than a covert dispatch path.
items.statement: PNC-012 supplies a rich candidate contract and a clear non-executable, non-dispatchable state invariant.
items.title: NodeSeed candidates have a fail-closed promotion boundary

evidence.exact_quote: NodeSeed routing metadata preserves effort_class, capability_lane, and capability_requirements alongside work_type, gui_related, frontend_related, and reasoning_tier before any reviewable candidate can be promoted to a WorkGraph draft.

items.impact: Different producers can assign gui_related and frontend_related inconsistently, changing model routing, review, and visual-evidence requirements for the same source PlanUnit.
items.statement: PNC-012 requires both gui_related and frontend_related but defines inheritance only for gui_related and gives no derivation or conflict rule for frontend_related.
items.title: Frontend and GUI routing flags can diverge

evidence.exact_quote: - WorkGraph drafts remain reviewable and cannot dispatch before Executor intake.

items.impact: The first executable-shaped artifact remains non-dispatched until an independently owned intake validates it.
items.statement: PNC-013 establishes WorkGraph draft review, WorkNodeRequest drafting, test binding, ordering metadata, and Executor intake as distinct stages.
items.title: WorkGraph drafting cannot bypass Executor intake

evidence.exact_quote: - Do not persist execution_unit_context payloads without schema_version or with secrets, tokens, passwords, credentials, API keys, provider auth values, or local machine secrets.

items.impact: Receipts, logs, screenshots, diffs, evidence refs, and source-control artifacts may contain credentials, personal paths, proprietary content, or user data even if execution_unit_context itself is sanitized.
items.statement: PNC-014 prohibits secrets in execution_unit_context but does not specify redaction, classification, retention, access, or deletion rules for the much broader receipt and evidence chain it requires.
items.title: Handoff evidence lacks a privacy lifecycle contract

evidence.exact_quote: | H-009 | Accepted request to dispatch receipt | accepted request plus preflight/model/test refs | WorkNode dispatch receipt | Executor scheduler/runtime | WorkNode executor | Executor_Protocol | dispatch boundary, capacity, model, authority, test binding | worknode_dispatch_receipt | worknode_dispatch_receipt | requeue after transient capacity or model issue | cancel dispatch before mutation or restore safe point | unavailable model/tool, authority block, or capacity exhaustion | dispatch ref, model ref, preflight ref, test binding ref | EP-099, EP-100, EP-101, EP-103 |

items.impact: A cancel, timeout, or retry racing with the executor's first mutation can produce duplicate execution or mutation after cancellation unless dispatch acceptance and mutation-start are atomically fenced and idempotent.
items.statement: H-009 names cancellation before mutation and restoration after mutation but does not define the atomic transition, lease, fencing token, or duplicate-delivery behavior at that boundary.
items.title: Dispatch cancellation has an unfenced mutation race

evidence.exact_quote: bounded worklists, assignment receipts, source hashes, currentness status, blockers, repairs, artifacts, retries, cancellation, supersession, and exact next action across context and process restarts. Changes after approval create successor ApprovedPlanPack versions; during compilation or execution a PlanDiffImpactReport classifies unaffected, already safe, needs recompile, and invalidated lanes and only continues unaffected work when dependencies and write surfaces prove safety. The PlanUnit index/readiness Goal regenerates only allowed Plans/.plan_index outputs, reports exact blockers, and creates no WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, candidates, executable queues, implementation files, or production tasks.'

items.impact: Persisted progress and currentness comparison support safe restart and bounded invalidation instead of replaying stale assumptions.
items.statement: PNC-015 defines durable restart state, hash-bound approved context, successor packs, and PlanDiffImpactReport-based partial continuation.
items.title: Runtime v2 has explicit currentness and restart recovery

evidence.exact_quote: block with a typed runtime-capability error, but it may not silently substitute one broad agent for mandatory parallel analysis or review.

items.impact: Without a deterministic sharding formula, capacity policy, timeout/quorum semantics, and write-conflict fence, compliant controllers can produce materially different coverage or deadlock under load.
items.statement: PNC-016 requires mandatory parallel work and typed write-conflict serialization but does not define how minimum assignments are derived, how partial worker failure is adjudicated, or how conflicting results are deterministically merged.
items.title: Mandatory parallel stages lack complete control semantics

evidence.exact_quote: every activation step, greenfield Git, non-Git FileSafe, dirty repository, remote SSH, optional GitHub or PR, missing harness, testing override, plan revision during compile and execution, cancellation before and after mutation, missing parallel receipts, and a deliberately introduced incomplete item. Ledger-to-Plans compilation writes or updates canonical Plans and allowed PlanUnit indexes only in their proper phases; it does not start Plan Compile, create WorkNodes, launch GoalRuns, modify implementation code, or start an Orchestrator build.'

items.impact: The fixture suite is falsifiable across idempotency, restart, repository modes, cancellation, parallelism, and incomplete-content detection.
items.statement: PNC-017 names a broad clean-room lifecycle oracle and concrete negative scenarios rather than accepting static contract presence as completion.
items.title: Clean-room fixture covers major lifecycle failures

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'Implementation readiness for PRD Builder, Planning Wizard, Plan Compile, WorkNodeRequest, Executor activation, and Orchestrator launch depends on the strict runtime contract packet in Plans/prd_planning_runtime_contracts.json plus the shared handoff schema in Plans/plans_to_code_handoff.schema.json. The runtime contract packet instantiates stage-specific Plan Compile cards, Native Ledger Service operations, discriminated ProjectContextSnapshot variants, PRD source projection and extraction records, Planning topic-map operations, WorkNodeRecord and attempt records, activation state/outbox records, visible testing records, typed UI command contracts, clean-room positive and negative scenarios, and retired Chain Wizard search exclusions. The standard run-gates include scripts/pm-prd-planning-runtime-validate.py so unresolved local schema refs, generic stage algorithms, impossible terminal success records, empty valid WorkGraphs, zero-request certified compiles, false-integrity activation, no-evidence visible test passes, and current-name-as-legacy tautologies cannot be used as certification evidence. node_compile_hint.create_worknodes=false in bootstrap PlanUnits means no WorkNodes are emitted during planning/governance compiles; it does not exclude accepted product requirements from later native Plan Compile once runtime enablement evidence, strict contracts, and executor intake are available.'

items.impact: A false gui_related value can prevent GUI-capable routing and visual/accessibility validation from following requirements that explicitly govern UI commands, visible testing, and Orchestrator launch.
items.statement: PNC-018 is marked gui_related false even though its canonical contract explicitly owns typed UI command contracts, visible testing records, PRD Builder, Planning Wizard, and Orchestrator launch readiness.
items.title: PNC-018 GUI classification conflicts with its scope

evidence.exact_quote: The node-readiness report must remain blocked until either runtime is intentionally disabled or the executable certification harness has passed and recorded evidence for the enabled runtime boundary.'

items.impact: This alternative conflicts with PNC-021's rule that hard-disabled status and incomplete executable certification keep buildability blocked, so the intentionally disabled state has no unambiguous result.
items.statement: PNC-019 treats intentional runtime disablement as an alternative to harness evidence without defining whether the result is blocked, ready, non-applicable, or buildable.
items.title: PNC-019 leaves intentional-disablement status unresolved

evidence.exact_quote: - Runtime conformance proof is not required for the disabled future compiler boundary.

items.impact: Future discovery references remain lineage and conformance expectations without becoming current readiness evidence or execution permission.
items.statement: PNC-020 explicitly excludes future discovery references from current runtime conformance and compile readiness.
items.title: Future discovery intake is correctly non-authoritative

segments.summary: Reviewed the readiness boundary, metadata and capability inputs, NodeSeed schema authority, buildability gate, bootstrap authority, and readiness status contract; found conflicting retry-route shapes and contradictory intentional-disablement semantics.

Reviewed GUI routing, native Goal handoff, readiness fields, compiler algorithm and Orchestrator boundary, durable design-only state, and stage cards; found missing GUI-route failure behavior, invisible-handoff observability, the retry-route conflict, and stage-registry migration semantics.

Reviewed NodeSeed candidates, WorkGraph and WorkNodeRequest promotion, the handoff schema and all H-001 through H-018 matrix rows; found GUI/frontend flag ambiguity, missing evidence privacy lifecycle, and an unfenced dispatch-cancellation race.

Reviewed runtime v2 currentness, parallel stage controls, clean-room fixtures, runtime contract readiness, and executable certification; found incomplete parallel-stage control semantics, inconsistent GUI classification, and unresolved intentional-disablement status.
Reviewed the future-only discovery WorkNode intake boundary and confirmed it does not grant current runtime readiness or creation authority.
